note: 'she turned around and saw Jesus standing there. But she did not recognize that it was Jesus.' (John 20:14). **She recognises him when he says her name** -- 'Jesus said to her, Mary.' (20:16) -- and not before.; 'Suddenly Jesus met them and said, Greetings!' (Matt 28:9), the women of 28:1 being Mary Magdalene and the other Mary.
'by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples' (John 21:1); the scene turns on Peter at 21:15.
'Jesus came and stood among them ... Then Jesus said to Thomas, Put your finger here and look at My hands' (John 20:26-27), eight days after the appearance Thomas missed (20:24).

'Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.' (John 20:19), and again by the sea of Tiberias (21:1).; 'Meanwhile, the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had designated. When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted' (Matt 28:16-17). **Eleven, and the doubt is recorded in the same breath as the worship.**

'Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these? ... Feed My lambs' (John 21:15), asked three times and answered three times (21:15-17), against the three denials of 13:38. **The text does not draw the parallel**; the count is simply the same.; "Come, follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men"
'One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side' (John 13:23), recalled at 21:20 as 'He was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper'.

'He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him' (John 13:5), explained at 13:12-15: 'I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.'

'Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.' (John 13:38), answering Peter's 'I will lay down my life for You' (13:37).; 'when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go' (John 21:18), and the narrator supplies the key: 'Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God' (21:19). **One of the few places a gospel explains its own figure outright.**
'Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee' (John 21:2) -- the last list of names in the gospel.

'the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus' (John 13:2), And when Judas had taken the morsel 'Satan entered into him' (13:27). **The chapter names the devil and Satan in the same scene**, which is one of the places the corpus treats the two as one.
